text.en:
To adopt the Constitution of the Lao People's Democratic Republic
(Amended Version 2025) by a vote of more than two-thirds of the total number of
National Assembly members attending the session.

This Resolution shall enter into force from the date of signature.

                                    President of the National Assembly

                                    [Seal and signature]

                                    Dr. Saysomphone Phomvihane


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
[Page 3]  CONSTITUTION — PREAMBLE
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Lao People's Democratic Republic
Peace  Independence  Democracy  Unity  Prosperity

National Assembly                            No. 77/NA
                                             Vientiane Capital, 20 March 2025

                    CONSTITUTION
                        OF THE
      LAO PEOPLE'S DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC
              (Amended Version 2025)

                             PREAMBLE

    From time immemorial the Lao people and their ancestors have lived and
multiplied on this beloved land. From the middle of the fourteenth century
onwards, our forebears — in particular King Fa Ngum — led our people to found
and build the Lao Kingdom of Lan Xang, making it unified, prosperous and
renowned.

    From the eighteenth century onwards, the Lao land fell under the domination
of foreign colonialists and their henchmen, who divided and invaded it. Our
people nevertheless upheld the heroic and unyielding tradition of their
ancestors and struggled ceaselessly, in close solidarity, to recover
independence and freedom.

    From 1930 onwards, under the correct leadership of the Indochinese Communist
Party — at that time the sole party of the working class in Laos — and later of
the Lao People's Revolutionary Party, the multi-ethnic Lao people waged a long,
arduous and grievous struggle, sacrificing their strength, their blood and their
lives. They defeated the colonialist and imperialist aggressors and their
lackeys, abolished the old regime, and on 2 December 1975 founded the Lao
People's Democratic Republic, thereby winning independence for the country and
genuine freedom for the people.

    Having won liberation, the Lao people, under the leadership of the Lao
People's Revolutionary Party, have jointly carried out the two strategic tasks
of safeguarding and building the nation. In particular, the comprehensive
renovation policy, grounded in the Party's guidelines and in the realities of
the country and of the world, has enabled the nation gradually to emerge from
underdevelopment, to consolidate the political system, to develop the economy
and society, to improve the people's livelihood, and to build the Lao People's
Democratic Republic into a country that is politically stable, socially united
and harmonious, democratic, just and civilised, steadily advancing towards
socialism.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
[Page 4]  PREAMBLE (continued) — CHAPTER I
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    In this new period, the life of society requires that the country and the
society be administered and managed by law. For that reason the first
Constitution of the Lao People's Democratic Republic was adopted and promulgated
on 15 August 1991. In the course of implementing the comprehensive renovation
policy, with the solidarity of the multi-ethnic people and under the leadership
of the Party, the 1991 Constitution was amended in 2003 and again in 2015 in
order to fit the situation of national development, to guarantee the rights of
the people, to strengthen the state apparatus and to expand the legal system.
This 2025 amendment continues that step-by-step improvement of the Constitution,
reflecting the will and the aspirations of the multi-ethnic people in building
the country.

    The Constitution of the people's democratic regime in our country records
the great achievements won by the people in the cause of national struggle,
national defence and national construction — that is, in the cause of
renovation. The Constitution defines the political, economic and social regime;
national defence and public security; the fundamental rights and duties of
citizens; and the rules on the organisation of the state apparatus.

    The Constitution is the embodiment of the people's regime and of the law,
reflecting the broad views of the people throughout the country, clearly
expressed through long-standing practice and through the wide-ranging opinions
of the people, gathered by the National Assembly, which the people have elected.

    The Constitution is the fundamental law of the State and of the political
system, with the highest legal force. All laws and all acts of State
organisations, of social organisations and of citizens must be consistent with
the Constitution.


                              CHAPTER I
                          THE POLITICAL REGIME

Article 1. The Lao People's Democratic Republic is an independent and sovereign
country with complete territory, comprising the land, the waters and the
airspace; it is a single country of all ethnic groups that cannot be divided.

Article 2. The Lao People's Democratic Republic is a people's democratic State
whose power belongs to the people and is exercised by the people in the
interests of the people, and which is guaranteed by a political system of the
people, by the people and for the people. All State power belongs to the
people, and is exercised by the people through the political system whose
leading core is the Lao People's Revolutionary Party.

The right of the multi-ethnic people to be masters of the country is
exercised and guaranteed through the operation of the political system, in which
the Lao People's Revolutionary Party is the leading core.

The people establish the organisations that represent their rights
and interests, namely the National Assembly and the local People's Councils.

    The election of members of the National Assembly and of members of local
People's Councils is conducted in accordance with the principles of
universality, equality, direct suffrage and secret ballot.

    Voters have the right to petition for the removal of a person they have
elected where it is found that the person has acted contrary to the rights and
interests of the people.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
[Page 5]  CHAPTER I (continued) — Articles 5 to 9
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The National Assembly, the local People's Councils and the State
organs are organised and operate in accordance with the principle of democratic
centralism.

The State protects the freedom and the democratic rights of the
people, which no one may violate. All State organs and State officials must
publicise, disseminate and educate the people so that the people know,
understand and comply with the laws, regulations and rules, and must strictly
implement them in order to protect the legitimate rights and interests of the
people.

    All agencies and officials are prohibited from using their authority or from
coercing in any manner that causes damage to the dignity, person, life, spirit
or property of the people.

(amended). The Lao Front for National Construction, the Lao Federation
of Trade Unions, the Lao Women's Union, the Lao People's Revolutionary Youth
Union and other social organisations are the rallying point that promotes the
strength of the solidarity of the ethnic groups and mobilises them to take part
in the cause of safeguarding and building the nation. They serve as the link
between the people and the State, protect the legitimate rights and interests of
their members, and have the right and the duty to monitor and inspect the
activities of the National Assembly, of the local People's Councils and of the
members of those bodies.

The State pursues a policy of solidarity and equality among the
various ethnic groups. Every ethnic group has the right to preserve and to
promote its own fine traditions and culture and those of the nation. All acts
that cause division and all conduct that discriminates among ethnic groups are
prohibited.

    The State shall invest in and promote the economic and social development of
the ethnic groups so as to raise their standards.

(amended). The State respects and protects the lawful activities of
Buddhism and of other religions, of religious dignitaries, of monks and of
religious teachers. It mobilises and encourages monks, novices and religious
teachers to take part in activities that are beneficial to the country and the
people. All acts that create division among religions and among groups of people
are prohibited.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
[Page 6]  Articles 10 to 14
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

(amended). The State administers and manages society by the
Constitution and the laws. The organisations of the Party and of the State, the
Lao Front for National Construction, the Lao Federation of Trade Unions, the mass
organisations, the social organisations and the citizens of all classes must
respect and strictly implement the Constitution and the laws.

(new). The territorial integrity of the Lao People's Democratic
Republic is sacred and inviolable; no one may violate it. All acts that
endanger independence, unity, sovereignty and territorial integrity, or that
oppose the cause of safeguarding and building the nation, are strictly punished
by law.

The Lao People's Democratic Republic pursues a foreign policy of
peace, independence, friendship and cooperation. It expands relations and
cooperation with all countries on the basis of mutual respect for each other's
independence, sovereignty and territorial integrity, non-interference in each
other's internal affairs, equality and mutual benefit.

    The Lao People's Democratic Republic supports the struggles of the peoples of
the world for peace, national independence, democracy and social progress.


                              CHAPTER II
                   THE ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL REGIME

(amended). The national economy of the Lao People's Democratic
Republic is a socialist-oriented market economy comprising many economic sectors
and many forms of production, which are equal before the law, assist one another
and cooperate, and which are linked to the development of science, technology
and innovation, aimed at steadily raising the material and spiritual living
standards of the people.

(amended). The State promotes economic activity within the country
and invests in the development of production, business and services and in the
application of science, technology and innovation, contributing to
industrialisation and modernisation, so that the national economy grows strong.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
[Page 7]  Articles 15 to 20
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

(amended). The State promotes foreign investment in the Lao People's
Democratic Republic and creates a favourable environment for the introduction of
capital, modern and environmentally friendly technology, innovation, artificial
intelligence and advanced management into production, business and services.

    The lawful property and capital of investors in the Lao People's Democratic
Republic shall not be requisitioned, seized or nationalised.

The State protects and promotes the various forms of ownership —
State, collective, private, domestic and foreign-invested — in the Lao People's
Democratic Republic.

The State protects the right of ownership (the right to possess, to
use, to enjoy the fruits of and to dispose of property) and other related rights
of natural persons, legal entities and organisations in accordance with the law.

    Land, minerals, water, air, forests, forest products, aquatic animals,
wildlife and other natural resources are the property of the national community,
which the State represents in managing them in a centralised and uniform manner
throughout the country in accordance with the law.

The State manages the economy according to a market mechanism
regulated by law, strengthens the macro-management role of the central
authorities, and applies the principle of centralised and uniform management,
with responsibilities clearly divided among branches and localities in
accordance with the law.

(amended). The State promotes the protection of natural resources and
the restoration of a damaged or degraded environment to a sound and sustainable
condition.

    All organisations and all citizens must protect and conserve biodiversity and
the environment, and must use natural resources in a sustainable manner.

The Lao People's Democratic Republic pursues a policy of expanding
economic relations and cooperation with foreign countries, employing economic
links in many directions, with many parties and in many forms, on the basis of
mutual respect for each other's independence and sovereignty, equality and mutual
benefit.

(amended). The State attaches importance to economic development in
conjunction with cultural, social and environmental development in a sustainable and
steady direction, giving priority to the development of human resources.

The State attaches importance to implementing the national education
policy in order to build Lao people into good citizens with good qualities, knowledge,
capability and a profession.

    The State and society attach importance to developing the national education
system so that it has quality, and to creating opportunities and favourable conditions
for all people to receive education widely, especially people living in remote areas,
ethnic groups, women, children, orphans and disadvantaged persons.

    The State promotes and encourages investment in the development of national
education in accordance with the law.

(amended). The State promotes the preservation, protection and expansion
of culture that is the fine heritage of the nation and of the ethnic groups, in keeping
with the aspiration to advance human society, with progress.

    The State promotes the promotion of national culture, arts and literature, the
creation, management and protection of cultural heritage, historical sites and museums,
ancient objects and antiquities.

    The State attaches importance to improving and expanding the work of the mass
media in order to serve the cause of protecting and building the nation.

    It prohibits any act that destroys national culture, or the use of culture to cause
division among the people, to undermine the fine customs and traditions of the nation,
or to violate the laws of the country.

(amended). The State attaches importance to promoting intellect,
innovation and creativity in the work of research, study and application of science,
technology, innovation and artificial intelligence, and to protecting intellectual
property in parallel with nurturing and building scientists, in order to achieve
industrialisation and modernisation.

The State attaches importance to improving and expanding the work of
social welfare in order to protect and promote the health of the people.

    The State and society have the duty to build and improve the social security
system, the medical examination and treatment system for all and with quality, to
create favourable conditions for all people to receive health care with quality,
especially women and small children, needy persons and persons living in remote
areas, so that the people have good health.

    The State promotes and encourages investment in social welfare services in an
advanced and steady manner.

    It prohibits all public health services that violate the law.

The State and society attach importance to encouraging, promoting and
investing in the sports and physical training of the masses, including all kinds of
sports that are the fine heritage of the ethnic groups and international sports, in
order to raise the level of sports capability, to strengthen the physical strength and
health of the people.

The State and society attach importance to implementing the social
welfare policy in a fair and appropriate manner, especially towards national heroes,
veterans, retired officials, persons with disabilities, the families of those who
sacrificed their lives for the revolutionary cause, and persons of merit to the nation.

The State, society and family attach importance to implementing the policy
on the development and promotion of the advancement of women, and to protecting the
rights and legitimate interests of women and children.

(amended). The State and society promote, open up and develop tourism in
the fields of culture, history, nature and agriculture so that it becomes a tourism
industry with a unique identity and a strategic economic sector of the country.

    It prohibits tourism that causes the deterioration of the fine culture of the
nation or that violates the law.


                                Part III

                   NATIONAL DEFENCE AND PUBLIC SECURITY

The State applies the guidelines and policies on national defence and
public security throughout the country in all aspects; builds and improves the national
defence and public security forces to be strong, solid, regular and modern, imbued with
patriotism and love for the people, and capable of fulfilling the duty of protecting the
independence, sovereignty and territorial integrity, and the lives, property and labour
of the people, thereby contributing to the cause of protecting and developing the
country to be firmly strong.

(amended). National defence and public security are the cause of the whole
people and are the duty and obligation of every organisation and of every Lao citizen,
who must take part in the national defence and public security forces in order to
protect the independence, sovereignty and territorial integrity of the country, to
protect the lives and property of the people, and to guarantee social order and the
stability of the people's democratic regime.

    National defence and public security must go hand in hand with socio-economic
development and with the protection of the environment.

(amended). The national defence and public security forces must attach
importance to improving and building themselves to be strong and comprehensive, to
enhancing patriotism, to being the armed force of the people that is loyal to the
revolutionary cause, regular, well organised, systematic and modern, with high combat
capability, and to being the core force in maintaining national stability, social order
and the good order of society; and to opposing, suppressing and resolving dangers in a
timely manner.

    The State attaches importance to developing the foundations of national defence
and public security, comprising political ideology, leadership, tactics and techniques,
technology, equipment, and the raising of the level of knowledge, capability,
specialisation, morale and discipline of the national defence and public security
forces.

(amended). The State and society attach importance to implementing the
policy of looking after material and spiritual living conditions, and to implementing
the policy towards the national defence and public security forces in order to increase
their capability in performing the duty of protecting the country and maintaining
social order.

    The national defence and public security forces must be self-reliant, strengthen
themselves by their own efforts and build up their own strength in order to guarantee
the performance of their duties and to participate in building the country.


                                Part IV

             FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS AND OBLIGATIONS OF CITIZENS

A Lao citizen is a person of Lao nationality as determined by law.

    The State recognises, respects, protects and guarantees the human rights and the
fundamental rights of citizens in accordance with the law.

Lao citizens are equal before the law, irrespective of gender, social
status, level of education, belief and ethnicity.

Lao citizens aged eighteen years and over have the right to vote, and
persons aged twenty-one years and over have the right to stand for election, except
persons who are insane or of unsound mind, and persons whom the court has sentenced to
imprisonment and deprived of the right to vote and to stand for election.

Lao citizens, women and men, have equal rights in all fields: political,
economic, cultural, social and family.

Lao citizens have the right to receive education, to study and to develop
themselves so as to advance.

Lao citizens have the right to work and to engage in occupations not
contrary to the law.

    Workers have the right to receive training, to receive treatment when ill, and to
receive assistance in cases of incapacity to work, disability, childbirth and in other
cases as determined by law.

Lao citizens have the right to freedom of residence and movement as
determined by law.

Lao citizens have the right to petition, to lodge complaints and to submit
proposals to the State agencies concerned in connection with problems affecting their
rights and interests, or the rights and particular interests of the collectivity.

    Petitions, complaints and proposals of citizens must be considered and resolved in
accordance with the law.

Lao citizens have the right not to have their life, person, honour and
dignity violated by anyone.

    Lao citizens shall not be arrested, detained or have their residence searched
without an order of the People's Prosecutor's Office or of a People's Court, except in
cases provided for by law.

Lao citizens have the right to freedom of belief and religion not contrary
to the law.

Lao citizens have the right to freedom of speech, of writing, of assembly,
of forming associations and of demonstration, not contrary to the law.

Lao citizens have the right to freedom of study and to apply the advances
of science, technology and innovation; to create literary, artistic and cultural works,
not contrary to the law.

(amended). The State protects the rights and legitimate interests of Lao
citizens residing abroad.

    Lao people residing abroad are an inseparable part of the Lao national community.

    The State encourages, promotes and creates favourable conditions for Lao people
abroad to invest in, protect and preserve the fine culture of the Lao nation, to
maintain relations with their families, relatives and homeland, and to contribute to
the development of the country.

Lao citizens have the obligation to respect and to implement the
Constitution and the laws, the regulations on labour, the regulations on living and the
good order of society strictly.

Lao citizens have the obligation to pay taxes and duties in accordance with
the law.

Lao citizens have the obligation to protect the country and to safeguard
public security, and to perform military service in accordance with the law.

(amended). Foreigners, stateless persons and foreign nationals residing in
the Lao PDR have the right to be protected in their rights and freedoms as determined
by law; they have the right to petition, to lodge complaints and to submit proposals to
the agencies concerned; and they have the obligation to respect the Constitution and the
laws of the Lao PDR as well as those of the Lao people.

    Foreigners who have merit and who have made great contributions to the cause of
protecting and building the country have the right to be proposed for the honour of Lao
citizenship of the Lao PDR.

The National Assembly of the Lao PDR permits foreigners who are
persecuted for having struggled for freedom, justice, peace and the cause of science to
take refuge in the Lao PDR.


                                Part V

                            NATIONAL ASSEMBLY

The National Assembly is the body representing the rights and interests of
the Lao people, the highest organ of State authority, and the legislative organ which
exercises the role of upholding the Constitution and the laws, decides on the
fundamental and important issues of the nation, and monitors the respect for and the
implementation of the Constitution and the laws by all State agencies.

The National Assembly has a term of five years.

    Members of the National Assembly are Lao citizens elected in accordance with the
law.

    The election of new members of the National Assembly must be completed at least
sixty days before the expiry of the term of the National Assembly. In the case of war or
other circumstances that make it impossible to hold the election, the National Assembly
may extend its term, but the election of new members of the National Assembly must be
held within six months at the latest after the situation has returned to normal. If it
is necessary for the performance of the work of the National Assembly that the election
of new members of the National Assembly be held before the expiry of its term, it must
be approved by at least two-thirds of the total number of members of the National
Assembly participating in the session.

(amended). The Standing Committee of the National Assembly is the permanent
body of the National Assembly and performs the duties of the National Assembly when the
National Assembly is not in session.

    The Standing Committee of the National Assembly is composed of the President, the
Vice-President and members.

    The President and the Vice-President of the National Assembly are also the President
and the Vice-President of the Standing Committee of the National Assembly.

    The President of the Standing Committee, the chairmen of the committees and the heads
of the divisions of the National Assembly shall serve for no more than two consecutive
terms.

(amended). The National Assembly holds a regular session twice a year. The
Standing Committee may convene an extraordinary session when it deems it necessary or
when so requested.

    A session of the National Assembly shall be valid only when more than one half of the
total number of members of the National Assembly is present.

(amended). Resolutions of the session of the National Assembly shall be valid
only when they are adopted by more than one half of the number of members of the National
Assembly present at the session, except in the cases provided for in Articles 55, 67 and
69 and Article 121 of the Constitution.

(amended). A law adopted by the National Assembly must be promulgated by the
President of the State within thirty days at the latest from the date of its adoption.
During that period, the President of the State has the right to propose that the National
Assembly reconsider it; a law that has been reconsidered and reconfirmed by the National
Assembly must be promulgated by the President of the State within fifteen days.

    A law promulgated by the President of the State must be published in the Official
Gazette, except in cases where the law provides otherwise.

Issues relating to the destiny of the nation and to the important interests
of the people must be considered and decided by the National Assembly or its Standing
Committee.

(amended). The National Assembly establishes committees and divisions to
serve as assistants to the National Assembly and its Standing Committee in the
performance of their work, within the scope of their rights and duties.

(amended). Members of the National Assembly have the right to question the
President of the State, the President of the National Assembly, the Prime Minister,
members of the Government, the President of the People's Supreme Court, the Head of the
Supreme People's Prosecutor's Office, the President of the State Inspection Authority,
the Head of the Supreme Anti-Corruption Authority and the President of the State Audit
Organisation.

    The persons questioned must explain to the session of the National Assembly orally
or in writing.

Members of the National Assembly shall not be prosecuted, arrested, detained
or imprisoned without the consent of the National Assembly or of its Standing Committee.

    In the case of a flagrant offence or an urgent matter, the authority concerned must
immediately report to the National Assembly or its Standing Committee for consideration.

    The investigation and interrogation shall not constitute a reason for the member of
the National Assembly concerned to be absent from the session of the National Assembly.


                                Part VI

                          PRESIDENT OF THE STATE

(amended). The President of the State is the Head of State of the Lao PDR,
the representative of the Lao people both within and outside the country, the Chairman of
the Central National Defence and Public Security Council, and the head of the people's
armed forces, guaranteeing the independence, sovereignty, territorial integrity, peace
and stability of the country.

(amended). The President of the State is elected by the National Assembly by
the votes of more than two-thirds of the members of the National Assembly present at the
session.

    The President of the State has the same term as the National Assembly.

    The President of the State shall serve for no more than two consecutive terms.

    The President of the State has the Office of the President of the State.

The President of the State has a Vice-President of the State, who is elected
by the National Assembly by the votes of more than two-thirds of the members of the
National Assembly present at the session.

    The Vice-President of the State performs duties as assigned by the President of the
State and acts on behalf of the President of the State when the President is unable to
perform his or her duties.

    In the case where the President of the State is unable to perform his or her duties,
the Vice-President of the State acts in his or her place until the National Assembly
elects a new President of the State.


                                Part VII

                              THE GOVERNMENT

The Government is the administrative body with the duty of managing the
State comprehensively, and is the executive body throughout the country.

    The Government is accountable to the National Assembly and to the President of the
State.

The Government is composed of the Prime Minister, the Deputy Prime Ministers,
the Ministers and the heads of ministry-equivalent organisations.

    The Government has the same term as the National Assembly. Members of the Government
shall serve for no more than two consecutive terms.

(amended). The Prime Minister is the head of the Government and acts on behalf
of the Government; leads and directs the work of the Government and of local
administrative organisations; appoints, transfers or removes Deputy Ministers, heads of
ministry-equivalent organisations, heads of departments, deputy heads of departments and
heads of divisions; appoints, transfers or removes the chairmen of the governing boards
of the capital and of the provinces after approval by the provincial people's assembly;
and proposes the promotion, demotion or reduction in rank of generals of the national
defence and public security forces.

(amended). The Deputy Prime Ministers assist the Prime Minister in leading the
work of the Government and of local administrative organisations, and are responsible for
certain work as assigned by the Prime Minister.

    A Deputy Prime Minister acts in place of the Prime Minister when the Prime Minister is
unable to perform his or her duties.

Ministers and heads of ministry-equivalent organisations have the duty to
implement and to organise the implementation of the resolutions of the sessions of the
National Assembly, of the Standing Committee of the National Assembly and of the
Government; to guide, manage and inspect the work of the sectors and organisations under
their responsibility; and to cooperate with foreign countries in treaties and agreements
in accordance with the decisions of the Government.

A member of the Government or all the members of the Government may be
subjected to a vote of no confidence by the National Assembly if the Standing Committee
or at least one-fifth of the total number of members of the National Assembly so proposes.

    In the case where a member of the Government or all the members of the Government is
subjected to a vote of no confidence by the National Assembly, the President of the State
has the right to propose that the National Assembly reconsider the matter, or to decide to
dismiss that person or those persons.


                                Part VIII

                     LOCAL PEOPLE'S ASSEMBLIES

(amended). Local people's assemblies are the bodies representing the rights and
interests of the local people, are organs of local State authority, exercise the right to
decide, consider and approve general binding regulations, decide on the fundamental
issues of the locality, and monitor the work of State agencies in the locality.

    Local people's assemblies are established according to the levels of local
administration, which comprise the provincial, district and sub-district people's
assemblies. As for the sub-district and village levels, people's assemblies at those
levels may be established by decision of the National Assembly.

    Local people's assemblies have the same term as the National Assembly.

(amended). The Standing Committee of the provincial people's assembly is the
permanent body of the provincial people's assembly and performs the duties of the
provincial people's assembly when it is not in session.

    The Standing Committee of the provincial people's assembly is composed of the
President, the Vice-President and members.

    The President and the Vice-President of the provincial people's assembly are also the
President and the Vice-President of the Standing Committee of the provincial people's
assembly.

    The President of the Standing Committee, the chairmen of the committees and the head of
the office of the provincial people's assembly shall serve for no more than two
consecutive terms.

(amended). The provincial people's assembly holds a regular session twice a
year. The Standing Committee of the provincial people's assembly may convene an
extraordinary session when it deems it necessary or when so requested.

    A session of the provincial people's assembly shall be valid only when more than one
half of the total number of members of the provincial people's assembly is present.

Resolutions of the session of the provincial people's assembly shall be valid
only when adopted by more than one half of the number of members of the provincial
people's assembly present at the session.

(amended). The provincial people's assembly establishes committees and
divisions to serve as assistants to the provincial people's assembly and its Standing
Committee in the performance of their work, within the scope of their rights and duties.

(amended). Members of the provincial people's assembly have the right to
question the chairman of the governing board of the capital and of the province; the heads
of sectors and the heads of ministry-equivalent organisations at the provincial level; the
chairman of the governing board of the city and of the municipality; the President of the
People's Court and the head of the People's Prosecutor's Office of the capital and of the
province; the President of the regional audit organisation; the President of the State
Inspection Authority at the provincial level; and the head of the anti-corruption authority
at the provincial level.

    The persons questioned must explain to the session of the provincial people's assembly
orally or in writing.

(amended). Members of the provincial people's assembly shall not be prosecuted,
arrested, detained or imprisoned without the consent of the provincial people's assembly or
of its Standing Committee.

    In the case of a flagrant offence or an urgent matter, the authority concerned must
immediately report to the provincial people's assembly or its Standing Committee for
consideration.

    The investigation and interrogation shall not constitute a reason for the member of the
provincial people's assembly concerned to be absent from the session of the provincial
people's assembly.


                                Part IX

                     LOCAL ADMINISTRATIVE ORGANISATIONS

(amended). The Lao PDR divides the work of local administration into three
levels, namely the provincial, district and sub-district levels.

    As for the village, it is a grassroots organisational unit.

(amended). Local administrative organisations are local administrative bodies
with the duty of managing the State comprehensively, and are a component of the local
administration structure.

    Local administrative organisations are accountable to the Government and to the local
people's assembly.

    Local administrative organisations comprise the governing boards at the provincial,
district and sub-district levels.

    The governing board at each level is composed of a chairman, vice-chairmen and members.

    The governing board at each level has the same term as the local people's assembly.

(amended). The people's courts are judicial organs; only the people's courts
have the authority to consider and adjudicate cases and to give judgment in the Lao PDR.

    The people's courts decide cases at first instance, on appeal and on cassation.

    The people's courts have the duty to protect justice, human rights, the people's
democratic regime, the interests of the State and of the collectivity, and the legitimate
rights and interests of individuals, legal entities and organisations in accordance with
the law.

(amended). The people's courts of the Lao PDR comprise the People's Supreme
Court, the local people's courts and the military courts as determined by law.

    When necessary, specialised courts may be established by sector, by decision of the
Standing Committee of the National Assembly.

(amended). The People's Supreme Court is the highest adjudicating organ of the
Lao PDR.

    The People's Supreme Court inspects and supervises the adjudication of the people's
courts and manages the judgments of the courts effectively.

(amended). The President of the People's Supreme Court is elected or removed by
the National Assembly, has the same term as the National Assembly and shall serve for no
more than two consecutive terms.

    The Deputy President of the People's Supreme Court is appointed, transferred or removed
by the President of the State.

    The head of the organisational bodies of the People's Supreme Court and the judges of
the people's courts are appointed, transferred or removed by the Standing Committee of the
National Assembly.

(amended). The people's courts consider and decide cases collectively and give
judgments on the basis of the majority, as determined by law, except for cases tried by a
single judge.

    In considering and deciding cases, the judges must be independent and comply only with
the law.

The trial of cases in court sessions must be conducted openly, except in cases
where the law provides otherwise.

(amended). The parties have the right to defend themselves in the conduct of
the case.

    The accused has the right to defend himself or herself, to contest the accusation or
the charge brought against him or her, by himself or herself, through a defence counsel or
through a lawyer.

    Lawyers have the right to provide legal assistance to the parties and to the accused.

(amended). Representatives of social organisations and citizens have the right to
participate in the conduct of court proceedings as determined by law.

(amended). The judgments of the people's courts that have become final must be
respected by all State organisations, mass organisations, the Lao Front for National
Development, the Lao Veterans' Union, mass organisations, social organisations, religious
organisations and all citizens.

    Individuals, legal entities and organisations concerned must implement them strictly.

(amended). The people's prosecutor's offices are the organisations that
prosecute accused persons before the court, and that monitor and inspect the respect for
and implementation of the law in the conduct of cases in accordance with the procedure of
law.

The people's prosecutor's offices of the Lao PDR comprise the Supreme People's
Prosecutor's Office, the local people's prosecutor's offices and the military prosecutor's
offices as determined by law.

(amended). The Head of the Supreme People's Prosecutor's Office leads and
directs the work of the people's prosecutor's offices at all levels.

(amended). The Head of the Supreme People's Prosecutor's Office is elected or
removed by the National Assembly, has the same term as the National Assembly and shall
serve for no more than two consecutive terms.

    The Deputy Head of the Supreme People's Prosecutor's Office is appointed, transferred or
removed by the President of the State.

    The heads and deputy heads of the local people's prosecutor's offices, the Deputy Head
of the Supreme Military Prosecutor's Office and the prosecutors of the people's
prosecutor's offices are appointed, transferred or removed as determined by law.

(amended). In the conduct of cases, the officials of the people's prosecutor's
offices must comply only with the law.


                                Part XI

                STATE INSPECTION AND STATE AUDIT

(new). State inspection is the work of the inspection organisations in
inspecting the implementation of policies, laws, legislative acts, rights, duties and
responsibilities of organisations and individuals, and in considering and resolving
complaints and proposals in accordance with the law.

(new). The State inspection organisations exercise the right to monitor,
inspect, suppress and combat corruption, and to consider and resolve complaints that
violate the law.

    The organisational system of the State inspection organisations is determined by law.

(new). The President of the State Inspection Authority is elected or removed by
the National Assembly, and is accountable to the President of the State and to the National
Assembly for the work of inspection, the suppression and combating of corruption, and the
consideration and resolution of complaints.

    The President of the State Inspection Authority shall serve for no more than two
consecutive terms.

    The Deputy President of the State Inspection Authority is appointed, transferred or
removed by the President of the State.

    The presidents and deputy presidents of the inspection authority at each level are
appointed, transferred or removed as determined by law.

(amended). State audit is the work of the State audit organisation in auditing
the management and the use of the budget, money and assets of the State.

(amended). The State audit organisation exercises the right to audit and to
confirm correctness, to propose remedial measures, to encourage and to monitor the
correction of shortcomings in audit work.

    The organisational system of the State audit organisation is determined by law.

(amended). The President of the State Audit Organisation is elected or removed
by the National Assembly, is accountable to the National Assembly and reports to the
President of the State, the Prime Minister and the Standing Committee of the National
Assembly on the work of State audit.

    The President of the State Audit Organisation shall serve for no more than two
consecutive terms.

    The Deputy President of the State Audit Organisation is appointed, transferred or
removed by the President of the State.

(amended). The State audit organisation has the following rights and duties:

    1. To conduct audits independently in accordance with the law in order to confirm the
correctness of the collection, expenditure and management of the State budget, of the
revenue and expenditure plans, of the reserve plans, of the debt, of the financial
statements, of compliance with the law, and of the implementation of the work;

    2. To manage, monitor and inspect the conduct of its own work and of the regional audit
organisations in accordance with the law;

    3. To report on its own work and on audit work in accordance with the law;

    4. To propose to the sectors concerned the application of measures aimed at remedying
the shortcomings found by the audit work.


                                Part XII

                          ELECTION COMMISSION

(amended). The election commission comprises the National Election Committee
and the local election committees.

    The National Election Committee is an organisation established by the Standing
Committee of the National Assembly, which then proposes to the President of the State to
issue a decree appointing it as the organisation with the duty of guiding the election of
members of the National Assembly, members of the provincial people's assemblies and the
local election committees.

    The local election committee is an organisation established by the Standing Committee
of the provincial people's assembly, which appoints it and declares it to be the
organisation with the duty of organising the implementation of the plan of the National
Election Committee in the election of members of the National Assembly and members of the
local people's assembly within its area of responsibility.

(amended). The election commission at the national and local levels comprises
a chairman, vice-chairmen and members.

    The term of the National Election Committee ends after the completion of the first
session of the newly elected National Assembly.

    The term of the local election committee ends after the completion of the first
session of the newly elected local people's assembly.

    The rights and duties of the National Election Committee and of the local election
committees are determined by law.


                                Part XIII

          LANGUAGE, SCRIPT, NATIONAL EMBLEM, NATIONAL FLAG, NATIONAL
          ANTHEM, NATIONAL DAY, CURRENCY AND THE CAPITAL

The Lao language and the Lao script are the language and script used
officially.

The national emblem of the Lao PDR is a circular shape; on the lower part
there is a half gear wheel with teeth, and a red ribbon bearing the inscription "Lao
People's Democratic Republic" on both sides, surrounded by ears of ripe rice forming a
hexagonal figure, with a red ribbon bearing the inscription "Peace, Independence,
Democracy, Unity, Prosperity" in the middle between the two ends of the rice ears; in the
centre of the circle there is a rice field, forest and a hydroelectric dam, and in the
middle of the circle there is That Luang.

The national flag of the Lao PDR is a flag with an indigo-blue field, red
stripes and a white circle in the middle. The width of the flag is equal to two-thirds of
its length; the width of each red stripe is equal to one-half of the width of the blue
stripe; and the white circle is four-fifths of the width of the blue stripe.

The national anthem of the Lao PDR is the anthem entitled "Lao National
Anthem".

The national day of the Lao PDR is 2 December 1975, the day of the
proclamation of the Lao PDR.
The currency of the Lao PDR is the kip.

The capital of the Lao PDR is Vientiane Capital.


                                Part XIV

                            FINAL PROVISIONS

(amended). The Constitution of the Lao PDR is the fundamental law of the
country. All laws must be consistent with the Constitution.

    The State determines 15 August 1991 as the National Constitution Day.

Only the session of the National Assembly has the right to amend the
Constitution of the Lao PDR.

    The Constitution shall be adopted only when more than two-thirds of the total number of
members of the National Assembly vote in favour.

(amended). This Constitution takes effect from the date of its promulgation by
decree of the President of the State of the Lao PDR.

    This Constitution replaces the Constitution of the Lao PDR No. 63/NA of 8 November
2015.
